scope: Gulf state waters, Southwest Florida (Venice to south of Naples)

species.name: Snook
rows: Whole until landed ashore. Hook and line only. Charter captain and crew may not keep a bag limit.

fed.note: Snook rules also apply in adjacent federal waters.

evidence: Slot Limit: Not less than 28” or more than 33” total length
Bag Limit: One fish per person per day

region.msg: This pin is outside the Charlotte Harbor snook region (26°15.2'N to 27°04.7'N on the Gulf coast). Snook rules differ by region.

species.name: Red drum (redfish)
species.bag: 1 per person per day, 2 per vessel
rows: Whole until landed ashore. Transport limit: 4 per person when traveling by vehicle away from the fishing site.
Hook and line and cast net only. No spearing, snatch hooking, or multiple hooks with natural bait.
Captain and crew may not keep a bag limit on a for-hire trip.

fed.note: Regional rules apply in state and adjacent federal waters per page; this region has the same limits.

evidence: Slot Limit: Not less than 18" and no more than 27" total length
Daily Bag Limit: 1 fish per person, 2 fish vessel limit

species.name: Spotted seatrout (speckled trout)
rows: May possess one fish over 19 inches per vessel (or per person if fishing from shore), included in the bag limit.
Same limits in the Sarasota Bay, Charlotte Harbor and Southwest regions.

fed.note: Regulations apply in inland, state and adjacent federal waters.

evidence: Slot limit: Not less than 15” or more than 19” total length
Bag limit: Three fish per person per day

species.name: Black drum
species.size: 14 to 24 inches (slot); one over 24 inches allowed
species.bag: 5 per harvester per day (may include one over 24 inches)
rows: Hook and line, cast net, seine, spear or gig. No multiple hooks with natural bait; no snatching.
evidence: Slot Limit: 14-24" with one fish over 24"
Daily Bag Limit: 5 per harvester per day

species.name: Sheepshead
species.bag: 8 per person per day (vessel limit 50 per trip in March and April)
rows: Hook and line, cast net, seine, spear or gig. No multiple hooks with natural bait; no snatching.

fed.note: State regulations extend into federal waters.

species.name: Flounder
rows: Closed every year Oct. 15 through Nov. 30.
Spears, gigs, hook and line, seine, cast net. No multiple hooks with natural bait; no snatching.

fed.note: Flounder regulations are for state and federal waters off Florida.

evidence: Closed annually from Oct. 15 through Nov. 30.

species.name: Florida pompano
rows: Hook and line, cast net, beach or haul seine only. No multiple hooks with natural bait; no snatching.
Permit and African pompano have different rules (see separate card).

fed.note: Page lists state and federal waters together.

species.bag: 50 per person per day. Vessel limit 50 (Sept. 1-Jan. 31) or 100 (Feb. 1-Aug. 31)

Hook and line, spears, gigs, seine, cast net.
evidence: Daily Bag Limit: 50 fish per person

forceCheckRegion.msg: Parts of Charlotte County have seasonal night closures for mullet. Check the FWC page.

species.name: Stone crab (claws)
species.bag: 1 gallon of claws per person or 2 gallons per vessel, whichever is less
rows: Up to 5 traps per person. Age 16+ must complete the free recreational trap registration at GoOutdoorsFlorida.com. Traps may be set 10 days before the season but not tended until it opens.
evidence: Minimum Size Limit: 2 7/8 inches; only claws may be harvested.
State Waters Harvest Seasons: Open Oct. 15 - May 1 (closed on May 2)

species.name: Blue crab
species.bag: 10 gallons whole per harvester per day
rows: Up to 5 traps per person. Age 16+ must complete the free recreational trap registration. New throat size rules apply.
evidence: Daily Bag Limit: 10 gallons whole per harvester per day

species.name: Spiny lobster
species.size: Carapace longer than 3 inches, measured in the water
rows: Last consecutive Wednesday and Thursday of July. The dates printed on the FWC page look inconsistent, so confirm them.
Landing or dip nets, bullynets up to 3 ft, hoop nets up to 10 ft. No spears, snares or traps.
A measuring device must be carried and used.
lic: Saltwater fishing license (unless exempt) (check whether a lobster permit is also required)
evidence: Minimum Size Limit: Carapace length must be larger than 3 inches, measured in the water.

species.name: Shrimp
species.bag: 5 gallons heads-on per harvester or per vessel
rows: Cast net up to 14 ft stretched; dip net up to 96 inches around; no more than two nets per vessel. See page for other gear.
evidence: All other regions (Southeast and Southwest) open year-round.

species.name: Sharks
species.size: Group 1 (8 species): none. Group 2 (7 species): 54 inches fork length
species.bag: 1 shark per person per day; 2 per vessel
rows: About 30 species are prohibited, including great hammerhead, lemon, sandbar, tiger and bull-type look-alikes. Learn them before keeping a shark.
Shore-based shark fishing needs the Shark-Smart course and a free permit.
species.why: Many shark species are prohibited. Identify the species and read the FWC shark page before keeping one.

species.name: Permit and African pompano
rows: The FWC page splits permit and African pompano by tabs and zones. I could not extract their limits reliably. Read the page.
species.why: Limits vary by species and zone. Read the FWC page.

species.name: Tuna, billfish, swordfish

species.why: Federal permits and special rules apply. Not reviewed.

species.name: Lionfish
rows: Harvest is encouraged. Special gear is allowed; see FWC page.

species.name: Unregulated species (jack crevalle, ladyfish, pinfish, gafftopsail catfish, whiting, cero mackerel, bonito and others)
species.bag: 2 fish or 100 pounds per person per day, whichever is more
rows: Hook and line, spears, gigs, haul seines and cast nets (some local limits). No chemicals, explosives, electricity, bang sticks or fish traps.
This default also applies to any species with no specific rule, but check the species-specific pages first.
evidence: Two fish or 100 pounds per person, per day - whichever is more.

species.name: Tarpon
rows: Fish over 40 inches must stay in the water. One record tag per person per year allows pursuit of a state or world record.
Special gear rules: no jigs with the weight hanging below the hook; Apr.-Jun. limits on lines and no breakaway gear.

fed.note: State and federal Gulf waters.

evidence: Tarpon is a catch-and-release only fishery.
